items.followUp: Explain why water has a higher boiling point than hydrogen sulfide.

rubric.why: Identifies the intermolecular attraction between water molecules.
rubric.description: Water molecules form strong hydrogen bonds with one another.
rubric.how: Award for identifying hydrogen bonding between water molecules.

rubric.why: Explains that overcoming water’s attractions requires more energy than overcoming those in alcohol, resulting in a higher boiling point.
rubric.description: More energy is needed to overcome these attractions than the intermolecular attractions in alcohol; therefore, water has a higher boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for a correct comparison linking the energy needed to overcome attractions to water’s higher boiling point.

modelAnswer: Water molecules form strong hydrogen bonds with one another.
More energy is needed to overcome these attractions than the intermolecular attractions in alcohol.
Therefore, water has a higher boiling point than alcohol.

rubric.why: Identifies the mobile charged particles present in a molten ionic compound or aqueous solution.
rubric.description: In the molten state or in aqueous solution, the ions of an ionic compound are free to move.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ions are free to move in the molten state or in solution.

rubric.why: Connects moving ions with the conduction of electricity.
rubric.description: These mobile ions carry electric charge, so the molten compound or solution conducts electricity.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that moving ions carry charge and enable electrical conduction.

modelAnswer: In the molten state or in aqueous solution, the ions of an ionic compound are free to move.
These mobile ions carry electric charge, so the molten compound or solution conducts electricity.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of reduction in terms of electron transfer.
rubric.description: Reduction is the gain of electrons.
rubric.how: Award for stating that reduction involves gaining electrons.

rubric.why: Requires an example that demonstrates electron gain.
rubric.how: Award for giving the correctly balanced reduction half-equation or another valid electron-gain example.

modelAnswer: Reduction is the gain of electrons.
